text: How Silicon Valley became a crucible for innovation, how the Swiss became a leader in watchmaking, how Singapore became a food haven – these are not plans drawn up by governments.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They happened because enough people were interested about something.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is organic; it is ground-up; it is haphazard.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have, therefore, embarked on a movement to harness the collective interests and aspirations of our people, develop varied paths for people to develop mastery and go as far as they can, regardless of their starting points.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But I must first, explain that SkillsFuture is not the $500 Credit granted to individuals, because I have gotten so many cuts on that.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Credit is a small but important part of SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It starts with schools, laying the foundation for our young; and then, higher education, that is, ITEs, polytechnics, universities, take over.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These help our young discover their interests and aspirations, impart knowledge to them, hone their skills and prepare them for the real world.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: From there, a lifelong learning system takes over, where they embark on a continuous journey of learning, updating and even finding a new path.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Along the way, they will persevere, improve and achieve mastery in their chosen fields, and maybe teach the next generation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If they do that, at the individual level, there is a tremendous sense of fulfilment and pride.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Collectively, Singapore becomes more competitive and more inclusive in the way we view success and merit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But beneath this learning infrastructure, what underpins SkillsFuture is the personal enterprise of each and every one of us, to learn a lifetime to achieve a mastery, a mastery that is a part of who we are.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, I will talk about what MOE is doing in three areas of focus as we move forward on SkillsFuture: first, interests and aspirations; second, developing mastery; and third, innovation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If we are learning something we are interested in, we are more likely to stay curious and engaged.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If we stay curious, we are likely to make learning that subject a lifetime pursuit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If we make it a lifetime pursuit, we achieve mastery.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, it starts with interest, or a deep sense of purpose and, as Ms Denise Phua said, a yearning for the sea.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is why we must make a greater effort to help students discover their interests and passions, through ECG.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling will speak more about this topic.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We then match student interests with their course of study as much as possible during the admissions process.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That, I fully agree with Ms Foo Mee Har.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, the polytechnics and universities are doing this to some extent.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have an exercise called the Direct Polytechnic Admissions (DPA).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Here, students are assessed through a range of measures, like interviews, write-ups and artistic portfolios, which cover not just academic scores but also other strengths, a much more holistic approach.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some secure a place in a polytechnic before they even receive their GCE "O" level results, a little bit like DSA.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Last year, as a pilot, we raised the cap for early childhood education courses from 30% to 50% and it worked well.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The universities also have some flexibility to admit up to 10% of students on the basis of their unique strengths and talents.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The effort to admit students into their areas of interest has yielded good results.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOE studies have looked into students with similar GCE "O" level aggregate scores.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, we have a control group, one group brought in through DPA; another group through the normal aggregate scores method, but both with similar GCE "O" level scores.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The students who are admitted to the polytechnics via DPA do better in their studies.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They have lower drop-out rates and are far more likely to embark on careers in the sectors which they are educated and trained in.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This confirms what had been intuitive to us all along.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When you are able to choose and enter a course you are interested in or feel passionate about, you feel more ownership and enthusiasm, and will likely do better.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If I may provide an imperfect translation, it means somebody who knows cannot match somebody who wants to know; somebody who wants to know cannot match somebody who loves or is passionate to know.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: At the polytechnics, we will expand the pilot done for early childhood education courses.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We started with the early childhood education courses out of necessity, because some of the students do not have staying power in the industry, something that Assoc Prof Randolph Tan mentioned.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When you hit the ground, when you see the kids, after a while, you might give up, because you really need to love to interact with kids and have a knack of doing so to be a good professional in the field.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are many other trades where similar considerations will apply, where interest, aspiration and some innate abilities, play a big part in ensuring that the student enjoys learning the specialised skills and has staying power in the trade.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some of these courses Page: 53 are baking, culinary, architecture, mass media, sports coaching, nursing, social work, drama and psychology, game design, interior design, digital forensics and so on.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will rename the exercise and call it the Early Admissions Exercise (EAE).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With this change, we will also wind down what we call the Joint Polytechnic Special Admissions Exercise (JPSAE), which covers a small segment of students today applying based on achievements, such as sports or community work.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the same vein, we will also put in place a new aptitude-based admissions exercise for students progressing from ITE to polytechnics.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) is already a heavy user of such methods.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Allocating places by grades on a single metric – aggregate score – is straightforward and, to many people, fair, transparent and objective.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But when you introduce other measures of a student's ability, it calls for an exercise of judgement.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Between a 12-pointer who is not so interested in a course but does not mind a course, and a 16-pointer who is very interested in the course, who do you choose?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This goes beyond making decisions based on one metric, but making a judgement call.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Notwithstanding the changes, every course will still need some minimum academic criteria, so that we have some assurance that the student can cope with the academic rigour of the course and we do not set him up to fail the course.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These changes can meet the aptitudes and interests of more students, but not all students.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There will be applications that the polytechnics will have to turn down, and I expect many more appeals.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And as Members of Parliament, you may expect more appeals.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And I fully expect them to quote what I have just said in their appeals.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I was somewhat apprehensive in wanting to make this move.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To be honest, I was asking myself: was I opening a can of worms?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But I became convinced that this is the right thing to do when I visited the universities and polytechnics and spoke to the senior educators.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They all told me this is so much harder to do but, speaking as educators, it is the right thing to do.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will keep a close watch on how things go and review thereafter.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I want to add a final comment on this topic, which is that, today, while many students have clear interests and pursuits, most are actually unclear about what they want to do.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We should not be pushing the young to rush into declaring their interests prematurely.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I will be rather upset if I change this policy and then see the sprouting of a new tuition industry teaching students how to ace interviews.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If a young person has yet to discover his area of interest, the system should give him more time for self-discovery.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If he cannot get into the course of study he wants, then I hope he can give Page: 54 what he has a chance.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Sometimes, we make the best out of the hand we are dealt with in life.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The creative arts is an area that many young Singaporeans are interested in.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have been working with the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA) and LASALLE, our two arts institutions, to provide good pathways for students.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I have asked Parliamentary Secretary Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim to take a closer look at this sector to see how our creative arts tertiary education can be further developed.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: While we expand the options for higher education, one specific area of concern raised by Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Ang Wei Neng is private education institutions.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Parliamentary Secretary Faishal will speak further on this topic.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The second area of priority is to build mastery.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It often takes our whole lives to master something.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programme (ELP) was launched last year, with the objective of opening a pathway for ITE and polytechnic graduates to deepen their skills within their discipline of study.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: ELP is a dual-track, work-study approach, where students can deepen skills and knowledge in school, while acquiring experience in industries.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is similar to the apprenticeship model of learning in Europe.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The feedback from employers and trainees has been encouraging.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will expand the ELP scheme in two ways.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, ITE graduates embarking on ELP obtain a Workforce Skills Qualification Advanced or Higher Certificate.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will introduce a new ELP pathway that will allow ITE graduates to work towards a full, part-time polytechnic diploma.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There will be two new ELPs along this pathway in the Air Transport sector.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are also looking into similar ELPs in the Public Transport, ICT and hotels sectors.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With this pathway, ITE graduates can take modules that are relevant to their current work first.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They can focus on upgrading their skills to do a better job, without rushing to get a paper qualification for its own sake.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also continue to strengthen the lifelong learning system.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Just as learning does not stop after school, the universities' role in education does not stop after students' graduation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: All five autonomous universities will be setting up new units dedicated to lifelong learning.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: NUS will set up the School of Continuing and Lifelong Education (SCALE).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: NTU will establish the College of Professional and Continuing Education (PaCE).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: SMU will set up the Academy of Continuing Education (ACE).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, the way to remember these is: all these will help you PaCE your learning, ACE your skills, and SCALE new heights!

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Singapore University of Technology and Design will also set up its Academy of Technology and Design, and SIT will name its unit SITLearn.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The purpose is not to offer part-time degrees or master's programmes to fuel the paper chase further, but to help workers stay relevant and competitive.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A key focus of these centres will be to Page: 55 look beyond traditional degree offerings by offering shorter, bite-sized certificate programmes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, in response to Assoc Prof Randolph Tan's question, all universities, including research universities, can participate in skills-based learning.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Through these centres, we also hope to underscore an idea pertinent to lifelong learning, which is, after you graduate, the next upgrade need not be a degree, masters or PhD.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Often, it is something, in real practical terms, to stay abreast of industry developments and changes in technology, or deepen existing skills.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In IT, this may mean getting a vendor certificate.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In aerospace, it may mean getting type-trained for certain aircraft or learning how to deal with composite materials.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If you are in the foreign service, it may mean learning a new language.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har pointed out in her speech that we also need companies and industries to be actively involved in lifelong learning.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The best way for companies to contribute is to offer real-life learning that institutions cannot simulate, a point that Assoc Prof Randolph Tan underscored.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Even the best graduates cannot be ready for work from day one.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They need time to learn about the industry and the company.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The partnership between IHLs and industries must, therefore, be an enduring and ever-strengthening one.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In Singapore, we have built up a landscape of private and industry-linked training providers through WDA's work over the years.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Whatever we have built up, we have to strengthen.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, training providers, such as the SIA Engineering Company's Training Academy, 3dsense Media School, SEED Institute from NTUC and At-Sunrice GlobalChef Academy, provide industry-relevant training which supports both employers, as well as individuals.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In logistics, Dr Robert Yap, Executive Chairman of YCH, is spearheading efforts to set up a supply chain and logistics academy – actually, it is called SCALA, another acronym.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) is planning to start an industry training centre for cyber security.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There will always be a place for these private sector providers and industry players in SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There is, of course, also the SkillsFuture Credit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is one part of SkillsFuture and it sends a very important message, which is that each of us is in charge of our own pursuit of mastery and learning throughout our lives.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is why only you can use your Credit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are at the stage of an evolution where we make every Singaporean think about their personal enterprise.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I heard friends who have parents over 80 years old thinking to themselves: what should I learn?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: At this stage, let us get that philosophical message through, rather than add more features into the system and over-administer it.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is for this reason that we have deliberately designed the Credit to be on the generous side.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We started with 10,000 eligible courses, not a small number, and included online providers, such as Coursera and Udemy.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Page: 56 If we accept this is a personal enterprise, then my answer to Miss Cheng Li Hui's caution about wastage and Mr Desmond Choo's request for guidance for workers to use the Credit is yes, let us make sure the courses are inclusive and of good standards.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Let us also leverage WDA and the Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) career coaches to give guidance.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But let us also have faith that individuals would make good decisions for themselves in time to come.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Give them some time, space and freedom to discover, wonder, imagine and make individual decisions.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Strike a balance, as Assoc Prof Randolph Tan has said.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Whatever people ultimately choose, we also need to suspend judgement a little.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Who is to say that an engineer will not find learning fine arts and appreciating the aesthetics useful?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Who is to say that a corporate trainer cannot learn photography, as Mr Baey Yam Keng had just cited?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Remember how Steve Jobs learnt calligraphy and how he applied that in the development of iMac and all the beautiful fonts we see today?

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng and Mr Desmond Choo asked for an update on the take-up rate of the SkillsFuture Credit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is a healthy number, not a mad rush, yet a good response.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will be working with the People's Association to roll out more SkillsFuture courses through the community centres.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As suggested by Mr Ang Wei Neng, we will expand the list of eligible courses over time.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Let us look at it, but I agree with the Member that it can be useful to many people.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Let us look at what practical steps we can take so that workers can use the Credit for genuine and useful executive or life coaching.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: SkillsFuture is not just about doing things skillfully.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It has much to do with innovation, because mastery begets creativity and invention.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is hard to innovate if one does not know a subject deeply enough.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: At the same time, knowledge advancement can also open up new grounds for new forms of mastery.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Before the Internet breakthrough, there were no expert influencers or masters in web design or e-retailing.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is why all advanced economies need research universities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The quality of research is the key determinant of a university's standing internationally.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Here, I want to make a comment about university rankings, in response to Mr Seah Kian Peng.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is a Page: 57 practical advantage for the students, especially when they step out to look for work.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But it is even more important when we examine why our universities have done well in rankings.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Having said that, rankings in themselves have no intrinsic value.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, Mr Seah Kian Peng is correct to have reservations about rankings.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Universities exist for a larger and better purpose.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We want our universities to make distinctive contributions to Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This must include the core priority of nurturing and developing our young, and this must include discovering new knowledge and techniques that can rejuvenate industries, create new opportunities and help Singapore stay ahead.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To fulfil these objectives, our institutions must have a global outlook.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The faculty will need to be diverse, bringing with them knowledge from all parts of the world.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Among them, there should be global top names to help us accelerate this process.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about the share of local faculty in our universities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is why MOE has been hesitant to disclose these comparisons.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But walk around the campuses of these top universities, you will find that you, too, will feel the diversity of the faculty.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Even if the data is not accurate, I think the sense is that they all have a diverse faculty.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Having said that, ours are national universities and there also needs to be a balance between global diversity and having a Singapore character in our universities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is a key balance to be struck and consistently and continuously fine tuned over time.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In teaching, the faculty must be able to teach students about Singapore and relate the subjects to the context of our part of the world.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I recently visited the Earth Observatory of Singapore at NTU, led by Prof Kerry Sieh, a very famous professor, formerly from Caltech.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The team there, which includes local undergraduates, is part of the global effort to monitor volcanic activities all around the world.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They hope to use the information to predict the next big eruption, give early warning and save lives.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I asked Kerry, "Why did you choose Singapore?" He said, "You are near the ring of fire, but not on the ring of fire, that makes you an ideal spot to do this research." I thought to myself: how exciting!

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Singapore has a natural advantage in volcanic research!

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Surely, if there are bright young Singaporeans interested in this, they can learn from Kerry and his team and, over time, contribute to the sector, the centre, Singapore and even humanity.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Another example – MOE provides competitive research funding open to university researchers, with evaluation conducted by an international expert panel for neutrality and independence reasons.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Earlier this year, I asked the Chairman of the Council, Prof Robert Brown, which was the largest research project that was awarded this year.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: He said it was a project on the Chikungunya and dengue viruses.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The actual name of the project is "Saliva-assisted transmission of pathogenic viruses by blood-feeding arthropods", dengue fever and Chikungunya, essentially.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If international experts recognise the importance of research on Singapore-relevant subjects, all the more we must have the confidence to build up our indigenous capabilities in these subjects.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Prof Tan Khee Giap is developing important knowledge at the Asia Competitiveness Institute to help Singapore gain in-depth knowledge of the economy around us.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Prof Lau Hoong Chuin heads the Fujitsu-SMU Corporate Lab.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They are using big data analytics to optimise traffic flows and reduce congestion in Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will nurture local academics who can produce quality work and contribute to Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The universities' human resource systems have to value and recognise them.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOE will be working closely with the autonomous universities on this effort.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: From here, higher performance of the machine is not pumping more fuel into the machine, and making it work harder, but instead, perhaps by rewiring and reprogramming it somewhat so that we optimise its performance and output.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have described Singapore's future as a mountain range of successes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we cannot assume that everyone wants to climb mountains.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I have a friend who recently went to Nepal and trekked the mountains.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: He spoke to his Sherpa guide and told the Sherpa, "You guys live in such a mountainous country.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: You must be a mountain people." The Sherpa replied, "You are wrong, we are not mountain people; we are valley people, we live in the valleys.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In fact, if you go up to the mountains too high, you can die from altitude sickness." We all have different destinations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some of us go to the village, some to the city, seaside, riverbank, oasis, all kinds of destinations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is a function of our gifts, dreams, resourcefulness and even luck.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We all find different paths to get there.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our children are growing up in a new world, striking paths into a Singapore that is more inclusive, all-embracing, a place where we can celebrate diverse talents and gifts.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Education must be at the heart of this journey, guiding them in purpose, equipping them with skills and helping Page: 59 them seize the opportunities of their age.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Parliamentary Secretary Faishal Ibrahim, you have only 20 minutes divided between the two of you.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: My colleagues have spoken about MOE's continued efforts to provide a holistic education that prepares students for lifelong learning.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We agree with Mr Kok Heng Leun in his Budget Debate speech and Dr Intan Mokhtar that the arts play a crucial role in this endeavour.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Arts education cultivates creativity, imagination, multiple perspectives and innovation; each trait is important in forging our future.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It fosters a deeper appreciation of our shared culture and heritage, and promotes social harmony.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Who among us is not moved with pride and a sense of belonging when we come together at the National Day Parade to sing "Home"?

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With expanded opportunities come a growing interest in the creative arts tertiary education sector.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Minister Ong Ye Kung has asked me to study this sector to see how we might improve on the current landscape and better position our creative arts graduates for careers that align their skills with industry needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also want to see how industry can contribute to deepening their skills.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I recently met representatives from arts institutions and polytechnics.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many shared that creative arts should be valued for how it develops the individual.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They highlighted that creative arts graduates find employment in industries beyond the creative arts, such as retail and manufacturing, because they bring with them artistic skills and dispositions that can be cross-pollinated to benefit different industries.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One such graduate is Ms Sasha Rafi who found that Ngee Ann Polytechnic's School of Film and Media Studies helped to expand her skills in creative thinking, effective communication and management of group dynamics.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These have been a significant help in her current role as head of marketing for the Singapore Grand Prix.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ultimately, we want these graduates to have good career prospects, contribute to the vibrancy and diversity of our economy and society and, at the same time, keep developing their passion, skills and love for what they do.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With more opportunities, students and parents need to make informed choices about the options available for further study or employment, including courses by PEIs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Page: 60 Concerns raised by some hon Members about the quality and relevance of PEI-run courses are valid as this private market sector is highly heterogenous, with uneven standards.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While CPE ensures PEIs meet minimum standards in corporate governance and course administration, it does not accredit or endorse the quality of their programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Going forward, we will study how to improve information transparency about courses and employment outcomes, enhance industry-relevance of PEIs and ensure regulatory requirements of CPE remain relevant.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The ongoing Graduate Employment Survey covers the nine largest PEIs, which cater for the bulk of private degree students.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will also study how more PEIs can offer industry-relevant training for continual skills upgrading and support manpower capability development in areas of industry need.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, PEIs, like SEED Institute and At-Sunrice, already offer relevant training for skills upgrading and mastery.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While we take these steps, students and parents must do their part to get all the necessary information before deciding which courses to pursue.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MOE's ECG efforts will help students assess their reasons and readiness to pursue further upgrading and if the course will help them acquire relevant skills for future employment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While I understand we have our own aspirations, I urge Singaporeans not to pursue qualifications as a paper chase but to develop their strengths, talents and skills.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Parental support is, therefore, crucial in helping our children develop the right instincts to make appropriate choices about education pathways, based on their passions and strengths.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As raised by Mr Zainal Sapari, the partnership among the home and school is critical in helping children discover and nurture these strengths and interests.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to support our educators and parents in their partnership efforts.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have developed two resources for this: a Parent Engagement Guide for Educators and a parent-child activity book for all Primary 1 students.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: If you have a child or grandchild who is in Primary 1, you would have received this.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I urge you to make use of this with your child.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also collaborated with members of our advisory council, the COMmunity and PArents in Support of Schools (COMPASS), to launch the COMPASS-Parent Support Group (PSG) Mentoring Scheme to build PSG leaders' capabilities in structuring and growing as well as sustaining PSGs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To support PSGs further, we are working with COMPASS to develop an online resource for PSG leaders.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This resource is developed by parents, for parents, and will be ready in the latter half of this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   Education prepares our children for a journey that requires them to undertake lifelong learning and master various skills.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Parents play a critical role in supporting our children as they grow older.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Give them the space and time to discover their strengths and interests and build a strong foundation of knowledge, skills and values that they can develop in their life.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Work closely with their teachers to understand their strengths, in both academic and non-academic areas.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: That way, you will be able to guide Page: 61 them better in making better choices for themselves.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Navigating the education journey is not always easy and it will be helpful if parents seek the support of other parents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Initially, his son was apprehensive about his father's presence and involvement in school.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: However, once he saw how his father was getting along well with his friends, he grew to appreciate having his father around.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Juraiman now better understands his son's interest in chess and feels much closer to him.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: According to Mr Juraiman, the PSG experience "has been a learning journey for me".

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: There are new types of courses in developing fields, such as app design, food technology, robotics and more.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This creates an array of diverse choices that can also be potentially bewildering.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Moreover, an individual's aspirations are likely to change with time and experience.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to help our students to navigate the complex universe of choices with confidence.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is a journey that our ECG counsellors embark on with our students, guiding them as their aspirations and experiences develop and mature over time.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With advice and assistance from the ECG counsellors, our students can then better understand their interests and strengths and make informed choices for their education and career path.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The guidance provided is not prescriptive; rather, it aims to enhance the students' self-knowledge for decisions that will impact their career.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng asked if counsellors know enough about what industries are looking for to effectively guide students to make such choices.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The counsellors also conduct regular industry visits and are in direct contact with industry sectors, chamber of commerce and trade and industry associations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With such access, knowledge and networks, the ECG counsellors are well-positioned to give timely and relevant advice on various career prospects.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They also heard from homegrown companies, like the Soo Kee Group and Home-Fix DIY.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, the counsellors are kept abreast of information on labour markets.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Their learning journeys to the respective sectors also arm them with close-up knowledge and experience.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This type of first-hand information, with interaction with the engineers and technicians, enable them to better counsel our students.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These career coaches, generally, have good industry knowledge and are well-placed to assist jobseekers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This move creates a multi-agency force working hard and closely together, linking the education front to the sphere of work very tightly, as well as with the various sectors of industries.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng talked about the heavy responsibility that the ECG counsellors have.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Our ECG Centres in MOE on Grange Road and in every polytechnic and every ITE college campus are fully operational and have been serving our students since the end of 2015.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Besides having the right guidance, getting wide exposure to relevant industries will help our young people gain a better grasp of what these fields may offer.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Hence, we will partner industries even more closely to provide systematic programmes that increase our students' exposure to industries at a younger age.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: One such initiative is the ECG Fair for Secondary 2 students.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The first ECG fair was held at Tampines Secondary School just last month.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: More than 2,000 students and teachers participated in the exhibition featuring various education and career pathways.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They attended career talks and also received practical hands-on experience related to the chemistry and life sciences sector.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For some of them, this really broadened their horizon and perspective.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: At the post-secondary level, we will strengthen our linkages with industries so that students will undergo meaningful internships and industry exposure.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Last year, MOE announced that the polytechnics and ITE colleges would be appointed sector coordinators for 17 sectors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: There are now 27 sector coordinators in total, covering areas of Singapore's future growth and priority sectors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: These new sectors are: air transport, design, electronics, energy and chemicals, environment management, human resource, landscape, precision engineering, sports and wellness, and tourism.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Last, but not least, I will now touch on the role and importance of our respective mother tongues.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In a fast-changing world, they put us in good stead by giving us a strong anchor to our Page: 63 heritage.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: (In Mandarin):   Bilingualism is the cornerstone of our education system, and it enhances our capacity in different domains.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, it strengthens our cultural and social identity and enables us to have a deeper appreciation of different ways of thinking.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It also helps us to maintain close connections with our neighbouring countries, allowing us to communicate cordially and engage in deep exchanges and trade relations.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We are moving forward in the right direction and will continue to support the learning of mother tongue languages in several ways for the next five years.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In 2015, the Prime Minister announced that MOE will increase funding commitment to the three Mother Tongue Language Learning Promotion Committees by about 50% in the next five years to $25 million.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: MOE will strive to provide an environment conducive for students to learn their mother tongue.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will continue to strengthen our partnership with the community, enhance current programmes, introduce meaningful initiatives and harness new technology and new media, so that the learning and use of mother tongue can blend more seamlessly into aspects of daily life.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For the Committee to Promote Chinese Language Learning, the Government will commit up to $16 million in the next five years to support the committee's work to roll out more exciting and diverse programmes.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We believe our students will develop a deep love for their mother tongue language and their culture.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: MOE will try its best to help these students develop a rich understanding of their heritage and values to strengthen the unique multicultural heritage of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: On the other hand, through education and career counselling, MOE will also equip students with a better understanding of themselves and provide them with up-to-date information about the opportunities available, so that they can seize these opportunities to create a brighter future.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: I have a question of clarification for Acting Minister Ong Ye Kung.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Previously, I was concerned that, with the efforts, the private training provider may be sidelined.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: But I am glad that the Minister has mentioned that there is always a place for private training providers.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: I hope to hear whether or not MOE plans to invest in strengthening some of our local-bred training providers like, SEED Institute for Early Childhood Education, and whether we will help them expand and deepen their capabilities.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: I was hoping that Minister could consider programmes with coaching involved in psychometric tests, like the Dominance, Influence, Steadiness and Compliance (DISC) or Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI), and if such programmes can be launched soon or put on trial.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On SEED Institute, as Members know, we have actually supported it for some years and, in fact, SEED was a very strong contributor in training Page: 64 early childhood educators into the market.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, it has been a very strong partner.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Of course, we cannot pre-promise further contract extensions but I think it has a strong track record of being a good partner.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I hope we can continue to work with SEED so long as it can continue to maintain its high standards of professionalism, governance and quality of training.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for life coaching, we will take in the Member's suggestions.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will consider it in a way that does not lead to abuse.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Which are the areas that will have the student care centres first?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: I ask this because, in very high demand areas, like mine in Sembawang, we need more after-school care services.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: So, hopefully, when rolling out, the Ministry could consider the local demand.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do need to make sure that the providers of the service have the staff with the ability to provide appropriate services and sufficient supervision to make sure that the children are well-looked after.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We take into account the suggestion that we should prioritise some areas and I will study it.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: Clearly, the Acting Minister did not open a can of worms but really open up a window of opportunity for many young people.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: So, Madam, I would like to ask the Acting Minister on real cases.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: For example, a resident who met me last night, for five years, he has tried to go into polytechnic, having completed his Higher Nitec.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: In that period, he has taken on roles working in McDonald's, Sushi Express, human resource, doing sales in a bank, all wanting to pursue a diploma in polytechnic to do business studies.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: These are all the qualities you would want.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I just want to sound a note of caution here.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Because the Member rattled off some things that he did.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When we talk about aptitude-based admissions, it is different from saying that you cannot meet the academic cut-off and, therefore, I take your sports and your community work into account and I deem that you meet the cut-off point.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That is what we call Page: 65 discretionary admission, to make up for a failure to meet a cut-off point.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That means, if he has really worked very hard on the ground over all the years, helping the disabled, the needy and the low-income and now he says, "I want to do a degree or I want to do a Diploma in Social Work", that is a consideration for aptitude-based admission.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: She never did a diploma before; worked in the food and beverage (F&B) industry for 17 years; now, being a mature worker, she wants to do a diploma full time and so she puts her name through the system based on aggregate score, in her case it is GCE "O" levels 17 years ago.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On that, she was sent to the nursing course.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: She appealed to me to say, "Why nursing?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I have been working in F&B for 17 years." So, we raised her appeal to the polytechnic.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The polytechnic interviewed her and put her into a Food Science and Nutrition programme, which is exactly what she wanted.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These are the kinds of examples that we hope we can have more of in future.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: I have a question for Acting Minister Ng Chee Meng about report cards.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: First, I would like to clarify whether this new style of qualitative report card is practised consistently throughout all schools at all levels because it does not seem to be the experience on the ground.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: The second question is: how can MOE also work with schools to clarify the mixed messaging that some parents are getting because I have heard of parents who are quite happy with the progressive report cards they are getting but, at the same time, they are also getting these assessment schedules, detailing extensively what is the weightage of grades and all that kind of stuff?

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: Their complaint is that they are both confused about what the system wants from them, the holistic assessment, and there is also an issue of distrust.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: They are not sure whether there has been a real shift at all.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: The third question is: I am aware that it is a work in progress, but is MOE working towards consistently connecting the non-academic competencies that they are tracking on these report cards to the desired key stage outcomes that MOE has listed?

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: This is because, for example, at the primary school level, one of the eight desired key stage outcomes is awareness of the arts and, clearly, there are not many primary schools prioritising this as a competency on a large scale.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The answer is yes, it is implemented across all schools and if there are instances where there is unevenness in the implementation, we would appreciate if the Member can let us know and maybe we can look into that.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: On the rest of the issues that the Member has mentioned, I do not have those details today.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: If the Member does not mind, I can take it offline with her to clarify those specifics.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The Minister mentioned there is no proven causal link between smaller class sizes and better educational outcomes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The Minister alluded to the fact we can generate good educational outcomes in Singapore based on tests like the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) and so on in spite of having larger class sizes than the OECD average.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: But we have to bear in mind that that is also with the help of the $1 billion tuition industry.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: My question and my suggestion are − and relating to the point about sustainability − right now, we have a situation where enrolments are gradually declining and, if we assume that the attrition rate remains stable and that teachers are not made redundant, would not this create an opportunity to redeploy teachers in such a way as to reduce the class size, to avail ourselves of those kinds of benefits?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: My second point is: just in relation to the increased emphasis on outdoor learning with OBS and so on, what are the provisions being made for students with physical disabilities in order to be inclusive towards them?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: What I said in the speech is that on class size, according to research, on a systemic basis, there is no conclusive evidence.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But we do go on a needs basis to tailor our education programmes for specific needs, whether it is GEP or for Normal (Technical) classes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, it is not just an issue of having a smaller class size for GEPs but according to the needs.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So long as they can meet the criteria of certain programmes, we would like to include them in those OE opportunities.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: How do the skills of Arts graduates from our polytechnics, NAFA or LASALLE meet industry requirements?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: And I understand that four more secondary schools will have the Enhanced Arts Programme.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Are there plans to extend or eventually introduce this to all secondary schools?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: My second clarification, Madam, is to Acting Minister Ng Chee Meng.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: I note that the Minister has not touched on reviewing academic streams in his response.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: But I would like to urge the Ministry to review academic streams in tandem with the PSLE review.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: I recognise that it is not easy because having the academic streams have made Secondary 1 posting and teaching a lot more expedient and targeted, but I think the timing is right.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: With five years or six years before the PSLE review kicks in, we should attempt to move away from this self-limiting sorting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Page: 67 Interestingly, I have the case of a student which I had no time earlier to mention during my COS speech.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, we can see the value of art education to our people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With regard to the arts education and graduates meeting the industry's need, you realise that when you engage someone who has those capabilities and that education journey, they are actually equipped with a multitude of skills.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For example, these skills can be transferred and applied to the various industries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They are able to think critically on certain issues and they also have this sense of aesthetics where they are able to innovate and create products, which I think is very useful.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I gave the example of Ms Sasha earlier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: She found that what she learned in her polytechnic became very useful in marketing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: That has somehow given her an edge and her employer, Singapore Grand Prix, found it very useful.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Another area is the user-experience design where, today, we see more and more companies, like OCBC Bank, the Airport SilverKris Lounge, as well as offices like HDB in Punggol, where they use such skills to innovate to enhance the user's experience.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Our Arts graduates would be able to meet such a need in the demand for the industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: All these are happening and you see the changing landscape not only in terms of what they can do but in terms of employment and job scope.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And of course, at the local arts institutions, we have enhanced internships for the students who can learn from companies and transit to working life better.

speaker: The Chairman
text: The purpose of clarifications is to seek clarification on the replies by the front bench, but not to add new points or to start another speech.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Yes, Mdm Chair, I would like to reply to Dr Intan's question to me.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But an equally important point in our education system is that, at the PSLE juncture, we would like to determine, after six years of education, how to tailor the secondary school curriculum to the needs of the individual child.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As we know, each individual child has different abilities, learning paces and learning needs.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: PSLE, together with streaming, has allowed us to place students into the appropriate courses to best cater to their learning needs.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I have joined the Ministry for about six months and I looked at the history of our education.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In the long past, we lost about 40% of our Primary 1 cohorts who started but did not finish secondary education.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, this tailoring, while I do understand some of the potential downsides, does have its important educational outcomes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Over time, the educators have also tried their very best to do different things to allow lateral transfers, across streams.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: These things that we are doing allow porosity.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We try our very best to afford the opportunities for the student to excel in whichever course he may be in.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This will always be evolving and we will be continuing to study the Member's proposals to see how we can further improve.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: One, a lot of the plans that were outlined by the Acting Minister is for what you do for the students and to the students.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: But I said in my sharing that I think the education sector is not immune to the changes of this world.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I wanted to hear the Acting Minister's views on what SkillsFuture plans MOE has for itself to address the new economy.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: How does the Ministry plan to help its staff meet these challenges and also adjust to these challenges?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Two, this is for Acting Minister Ng, on the PSLE review.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: It is definitely an improvement so that it is not such a fine score to work on.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: However, at the end of it, it still boils down to grades.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I am just wondering what the Acting Minister thinks will be the game changer or the key that will unlock Singaporeans from our habit of chasing the grades and chasing the scores through tuition and, definitely, wanting to go for a degree for that matter.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, I am just wondering how the Acting Minister feels about that.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: One is for teachers and, that is, at NIE.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: NIE has always been updating its curriculum and moving forward.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It has a big role to play in SkillsFuture to upgrade and deepen the skills of our teachers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: At the polytechnics and ITE, many of them come from industry and they have to continue this strong effort to make sure that there is a rotation of their lecturers moving between academia and industry.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That way, they keep abreast of what is happening in the industry and bring the lessons back into the polytechnics and ITE.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In universities, I actually spoke about this in my speech, where I shared research plays a big role because in our research universities, generation of knowledge is a core business and this is something we have to do better, especially for subjects relevant to Singapore and involving both global as well as local talent.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As a Ministry, we will be giving them time, space and freedom to decide what to study.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: There is really no easy straightforward solution, no silver bullet answer that I can give for cause-effect outcomes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As I have tried to articulate just now, it requires a collective paradigm shift involving all of us, what we do for Page: 69 the student, so on and so forth, including societal definitions of success, things that Acting Minister Ong Ye Kung spoke about.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, we do require a partnership with parents and students with the community and, ultimately, in the workplaces as well, on what would people eventually value.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: That is why in my speech I said that it would take time.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: MOE has taken some steps and we are taking bolder steps to review many of these structures and policies.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We want to take the step to reduce fine differentiation so that we, at least, free up some space for the students to smell the flowers, as I have mentioned.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: MOE, however, cannot do any of these alone.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We need all the different stakeholders to come on board with us, to value other areas beyond academics.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The three areas that I have spoken about, we should look at them in totality and embrace them to reduce the emphasis on academics, more emphasis on non-academic areas, including character and values, and also provide, over time, a realisation of the possibility of every school being a good school, to open up choices and opportunities for students to pick and choose schools that will best meet their needs.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I think this paradigm shift is needed and, again, I do apologise that I do not have a silver bullet answer, a simple one that will be able to move us into the realm that Ms Denise Phua has mentioned.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Let us not hire a whole new army every time we start a new scheme.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There is an existing group of people with the experience that we can use and leverage to deliver this service that Mr Desmond Choo spoke about.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And I think he has also just realised I have shot the arrow back to him.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: This is for Acting Minister Ng Chee Meng.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: While it is true that there is inconclusive research on the causal link between reduced class size and teaching and education outcomes on a systemic level, and that is because academics are so good at destroying at one another's research, there are provisional conclusive results that reduced class size would positively affect education outcomes for disadvantaged students, especially in the US and the UK.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Given this conclusion, and because the Minister said that there is a possibility of considering improvements to the class sizes, would the Ministry consider pilot studies on reducing class sizes in secondary schools, for example, in mainstream schools that have more students with financial assistance, to see whether results would bear fruit in Singapore?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: My second clarification is actually for the "Teach for Singapore" programme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: What avenues are there for teachers who are passionate to teach disadvantaged students to take a sabbatical to upgrade themselves with skills outside the regular academic fields so that they can go and teach the disadvantaged students and then, to request for a transfer, where can they go and teach the disadvantaged students?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Perhaps, I will just give an update to Assoc Prof Daniel Goh.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: When we do a needs-based approach, we provide the necessary resources to disadvantaged students.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In the time that I have been in MOE, if I recall the numbers correctly, about 6% of our students benefit from these programmes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: They do graduate out of these support programmes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, it is very tailored, as per our philosophy, where there is need, we will put in the necessary resources to level our children up.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For the posting suggestion that Assoc Prof Goh mentioned, when I visited Spectra Secondary School in Woodlands, I was very impressed by one teacher.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But because of her deeply ingrained desire to make a bigger difference to children with low progress, she decided to ask for a transfer to Spectra.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As I had mentioned in my speech, in the context of Singapore, through NIE, we have a central institute, if you will, to train teachers to a very high quality.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In this central system, we do allow these transfers for teachers with the passion that Assoc Prof Goh had mentioned.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
